blocks.content: The catalog above is a snapshot: it changes whenever Anthropic releases or retires models. `GET /v1/models` returns the list of models enabled for your API key at request time, instead of relying on a fixed table in your code or on this page.
It makes sense to use it when:

items.title: Dynamic selector
items.description: Populate a model dropdown in an admin UI without hardcoding or redeploying every time a new model ships.

items.title: Validate before pinning an ID
items.description: Confirm that a model ID is still current before saving it to configuration, instead of discovering in production that it was retired.

items.title: Detect new models
items.description: A periodic job that checks whether a newer model appeared, without relying on manually reading the changelog.

blocks.title: Not needed for normal use
blocks.content: To simply call Claude with a known model, `GET /models` isn't necessary — the `model` is passed directly in `POST /messages`. This endpoint matters only when the catalog itself is part of the application logic (dynamic selection, validation, availability monitoring).
Choose the model based on three factors: required speed, task complexity, and budget.

subsections.title: What it speeds up, and what it doesn't

blocks.content: Fast mode runs the same model with a faster inference configuration — it isn't a different model, and it doesn't change its capabilities. It delivers up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second (OTPS), but that benefit is specifically in generation speed, not time to first token (TTFT): how long until the first token arrives doesn't improve, what improves is how fast the following ones arrive.

blocks.code:
response = client.beta.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5",
    max_tokens=4096,
    speed="fast",
    betas=["fast-mode-2026-02-01"],
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Refactor this module"}],
)

print(response.usage.speed)  # "fast" or "standard"

blocks.title: Research preview, with uneven model support
blocks.content: Only Claude Opus 5 and Claude Opus 4.8 support it. Requesting it on Opus 4.7 returns an error; requesting it on Opus 4.6 doesn't error but silently runs at standard speed and bills at the standard rate — which is why it's worth checking `usage.speed` in the response instead of assuming `speed: "fast"` in the request guarantees it was used. Available only on the direct API and Claude Managed Agents; not on Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Google Cloud, or Microsoft Foundry.

rows: Incompatible with batch's async processing model
Two separate rate-limit mechanisms — they don't combine
Invalidates the prompt cache — fast and standard don't share cached prefixes
